skill.description: Analyze cloud spending and recommend cost optimization actions for AWS, Azure, and GCP. It covers rightsizing, reservations, storage, network, containers, serverless, tagging, budgets, and dashboards.
skill.summary: Optimize cloud infrastructure costs while preserving performance and reliability.

security_audit.summary: The skill is a cloud cost optimization guide with code examples for billing analysis, resource rightsizing, and dashboards. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, Terraform key and index names, snapshots, and cloud resource identifiers. Two low-risk findings are confirmed because sample dashboard HTML loads third-party JavaScript from public CDNs; no malware, prompt injection, credential theft, or covert exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Dashboard examples load third-party JavaScript from public CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact library versions with integrity hashes, self-host approved assets, or document that deployed dashboards require network review.

finding_verdicts.reason: The generated dashboard loads Chart.js from a public CDN, which creates an external network dependency and executes third-party JavaScript if deployed. This appears to support charting and shows no exfiltration intent, so severity is low.

The executive dashboard loads D3 from a public CDN, which introduces third-party script execution and a network dependency. The context is legitimate visualization, with no evidence of malicious collection.
The code reads MONTHLY_BUDGET as a non-secret configuration value with a safe default. It does not enumerate environment variables or access credentials.
The Terraform field references an EC2 key pair name variable, not a private key, certificate, or key file. No secret material is embedded or read.
The word key is used as a Terraform loop index in launch_specification.key. It is not a credential, certificate, or file path.
The key token is used to build a Name tag for spot instances. This is string interpolation for labeling, not secret handling.
The snapshot is created as a rollback step before resizing an EC2 instance. It is an expected safety control in the rightsizing workflow, not reconnaissance.
The snapshot identifier is returned as operation metadata for rollback tracking. It does not collect system data or transmit it externally.
The AMI ID variable is part of a Terraform spot instance launch specification. It configures expected cloud infrastructure and does not perform host reconnaissance.
The subnet ID expression selects a subnet from provided Terraform variables for spot instance placement. This is normal infrastructure configuration, not discovery or exfiltration.
The VPC ID is used while checking VPC endpoint optimization opportunities. Cloud inventory is necessary for this cost workflow and is not presented as covert reconnaissance.
The SQL join links cost records to resource tags for cost allocation. This is billing analysis, not system reconnaissance.
The backticks format a Markdown file path reference. There is no Ruby code, shell execution, or command invocation on this line.
The backticks format a Markdown file path reference in the resources list. This is documentation syntax, not executable code.

content.value_statement: Cloud bills grow when teams lack visibility into waste, sizing, and commitments. This skill guides cost analysis, rightsizing, reservations, controls, and dashboards across major clouds.
actual_capabilities: Analyze cloud costs by service, resource, trend, anomaly, and waste category.
Identify idle, underused, and oversized resources with estimated savings.
Plan rightsizing actions with risk notes, dry-run support, and rollback steps.
Compare reservations, Savings Plans, and spot instance options for steady workloads.
Recommend storage, network, container, and serverless cost controls.
Create budget, alert, tagging, and dashboard patterns for ongoing governance.
limitations: Requires accurate billing, usage, and resource inventory data from the user or cloud account.
Code samples must be adapted and tested before any production change.
Savings estimates depend on pricing, discounts, usage patterns, and regional availability.
Does not replace cloud provider, compliance, or finance approval processes.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Monthly Savings
use_cases.description: Review service and resource spend to rank quick wins by savings, effort, and operational risk.

use_cases.title: Rightsize Infrastructure Safely
use_cases.description: Plan instance, storage, and container changes with monitoring checks, rollback steps, and approval points.

use_cases.title: Build Cost Governance
use_cases.description: Define tagging standards, budgets, alerts, and dashboards that keep cloud spending visible over time.

prompt_templates.title: Find Quick Savings
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a monthly bill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this monthly cloud cost summary. Identify the top three waste areas, expected savings, and low-risk next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Rightsizing Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these compute metrics and resource sizes. Recommend rightsizing changes with risk level, validation steps, rollback plan, and monthly savings estimate.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Commitment Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these steady workloads for reservations, Savings Plans, and spot usage. Compare savings, lock-in risk, coverage gaps, and implementation order.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cost Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cloud cost governance plan for this organization. Include tagging policy, budgets, alerts, dashboards, review cadence, and owner responsibilities.

output_examples.input: A team shares thirty days of cloud spend grouped by service.
output_examples.output: A prioritized savings report listing oversized compute, idle storage, reservation gaps, estimated monthly savings, and recommended owners.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer provides CPU, memory, and traffic metrics for production instances.
output_examples.output: A rightsizing plan with proposed instance types, validation checks, rollback steps, risk ratings, and a phased rollout sequence.

output_examples.input: Leadership asks for cost controls before the next quarter.
output_examples.output: A governance plan covering tags, budgets, anomaly alerts, dashboards, escalation rules, and a monthly optimization review process.

best_practices: Start with read-only billing and usage analysis before recommending changes.
Validate every infrastructure change in staging and keep a rollback path.
Track savings after implementation so recommendations can be verified.
anti_patterns: Deleting or resizing resources without ownership, backup, and rollback checks.
Optimizing only for price while ignoring performance, reliability, or support needs.
Using old pricing assumptions without checking current region and commitment terms.

faq.question: Which cloud providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, and GCP patterns, with examples that users must adapt to their environment.

faq.question: Can it make production changes automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes implementation patterns, but production changes require user approval, testing, and rollback planning.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide billing exports, usage metrics, resource inventory, tags, workload context, and any current discount commitments.

faq.question: Does it calculate exact savings?
faq.answer: It can estimate savings from supplied data, but exact results depend on pricing, contracts, and future usage.

faq.question: Is it useful for FinOps reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports cost allocation, tagging, dashboards, budgets, anomaly detection, and recurring review workflows.

faq.question: How should risky recommendations be handled?
faq.answer: Use staged rollout, monitoring, owner approval, backup checks, and rollback steps before changing production resources.
